description: The image displays a series of five bar charts arranged horizontally, each illustrating a different distribution pattern of parameter efficiency in fine-tuning, as referenced in the paper “Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Design Spaces.” From left to right, the first chart, labeled “Increasing,” shows four light green bars of progressively increasing height from left to right, indicating a rising trend in parameter allocation or efficiency. The second chart, labeled “Uniform,” presents four bars of equal height, suggesting an even distribution across all categories. The third, labeled “Decreasing,” shows four bars of progressively decreasing height, reflecting a downward trend. The fourth chart, which lacks a visible label but is visually distinct with a gray rectangular overlay obscuring its label, displays a pattern with low bars on the ends and taller bars in the middle — resembling a “U” or “valley” shape, possibly indicating a central concentration. The fifth chart, labeled “Bottleneck,” shows a pattern with taller bars on the ends and shorter bars in the middle, forming an inverted “U” or “bottleneck” shape, implying constrained or minimal allocation in the center. All bars are rendered in a consistent light green color with black outlines, and each chart is separated by white space, with labels positioned directly beneath their respective bar groups. The visual design emphasizes comparative distribution shapes rather than precise numerical values, serving as a conceptual illustration of different parameter allocation strategies in fine-tuning design spaces.
